\begin{theorem}[Directional quenched law on finite prime support]
\label{thm:prime-support-directional-quenched}
Retain the notation of \Cref{prop:prime-support-interface}, and fix
\(\boldsymbol\rho\in\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\).  Put
\[
 g_i(z):=\frac{1-z}{1-p_i z},
 \qquad
 h_i(z):=\frac{z g_i'(z)}{g_i(z)}
 =\frac{(p_i-1)z}{(1-z)(1-p_i z)}.
\]
There are unique \(\tau>0\) and
\(\mathbf z=\mathbf z(\boldsymbol\rho)\in
\prod_i(0,p_i^{-1})\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \prod_{i=1}^d g_i(z_i)=2,
 \qquad h_i(z_i)=\tau\rho_i\quad(1\le i\le d).
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}
\end{equation}
More explicitly, \(z_i=\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i)\), where
\begin{equation}
 \zeta_i(x)=
 \frac{(p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x-
  \sqrt{((p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x)^2-4p_i x^2}}
 {2p_i x}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}
\end{equation}
The point \(\mathbf z\) is the unique point of
\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\) in the closed polydisc
\(\{|w_i|\le z_i\}\).

Give every letter \((\mathbf a,h/q_{\mathbf a})\) the probability
\begin{equation}
 \Pr_{\mathbf z}\{(\mathbf A,C)=
  (\mathbf a,c(h/q_{\mathbf a}))\}=\mathbf z^{\mathbf a}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law}
\end{equation}
This is a probability law, and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=2\tau\boldsymbol\rho,
 \qquad m_C(\boldsymbol\rho):=\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}C<\infty.
\]
Define its directional velocity by
\begin{equation}
 v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}:=
 \frac{2\tau\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i}{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-velocity}
\end{equation}

Let \(\mathbf n_N=N\boldsymbol\rho+O(1)\in\mathbb N^d\), and let
\(W_N\) be uniform among the nonempty free generator words of total exponent
\(\mathbf n_N\).  If \(R_N\) is its number of letters and \(T_N\) its
total cost, then
\begin{equation}
 \frac{R_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac1{2\tau},
 \qquad
 \frac{T_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}{2\tau},
 \qquad
 \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{T_N}
 \xrightarrow{\Pr}v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}
\end{equation}

Finally, let \(m_N\to\infty\) be integers such that
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{m_N}\longrightarrow
 \alpha\in[0,v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}).
 \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}
\end{equation}
Then the exact level
\(\{x\in X_{m_N}:d_{m_N}(x)=q_{\mathbf n_N}\}\) is nonempty for all
sufficiently large \(N\),
\begin{equation}
 C_{m_N}(q_{\mathbf n_N})
 \sim4\card{\{\text{free words of exponent }\mathbf n_N\}},
 \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-count}
\end{equation}
and, under the uniform law on this level,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{L(g_{m_N})}{m_N}
 \xrightarrow{\Pr}
 \frac{\alpha}{v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}
\end{equation}
The free-word convergences are uniform when \(\boldsymbol\rho\) ranges over a
compact subset of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\) and
\(\|\mathbf n_N-N\boldsymbol\rho\|\) is bounded.  The finite-window
conclusions are uniform under the additional requirement that the budget
ratio remain bounded away from one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each \(h_i\) is strictly increasing from zero to infinity on
\((0,p_i^{-1})\).  Solving the resulting quadratic gives
\eqref{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}.  Hence
\(\prod_i g_i(\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i))\) increases continuously from one to
infinity, which proves existence and uniqueness in
\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}.  Since
\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1\),
\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law} has total mass one, and
Euler differentiation gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}A_i
 =z_i\partial_{z_i}A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)
 =2h_i(z_i)=2\tau\rho_i.
\]

We verify the strict-minimality and lattice hypotheses needed below.  If
\(|w_i|\le z_i\) and \(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\), coefficient
positivity gives
\[
 1\le A_{\mathcal P}(|\mathbf w|,1)
 \le A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1.
\]
The support contains every \(\mathbf e_i\), so equality in the second
inequality forces \(|w_i|=z_i\) for every \(i\).  Equality in the triangle
inequality then forces all supported monomials to have phase one; applying
this to the \(\mathbf e_i\) gives \(w_i=z_i\).  The same support contains
\(2\mathbf e_i\), so its difference lattice is \(\mathbb Z^d\).  Finally,
the covariance matrix of \(\mathbf A\) is positive definite: if
\(\mathbf t\cdot\mathbf A\) were constant almost surely, comparison of
\(\mathbf e_i\) and \(2\mathbf e_i\) would give \(t_i=0\) for every
\(i\).

The fixed-denominator mean estimate quoted in the proof of
\Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{1\le h<q\\(h,q)=1}}c(h/q)
 =O(q(1+\log q)^2).
\]
Since \(p_i z_i<1\), summation over exponent vectors proves
\(m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)<\infty\).

We now apply the smooth strictly minimal point expansion of
Pemantle--Wilson \cite{PemantleWilson2002}; the preceding paragraph verifies
its nonperiodicity, strict minimality, and nondegenerate transverse Hessian
for the present rational function.  Marking each letter by \(e^s\) and
using the expansion uniformly for small complex \(s\) gives the usual
analytic quasi-powers estimate.  The critical number of letters is determined
by
\[
 r_N\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=N\boldsymbol\rho,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad r_N=\frac{N}{2\tau}.
\]
It follows that \(R_N/N\to1/(2\tau)\) in probability.

For \(M>0\), mark instead the bounded cost \(C\wedge M\).  The same analytic
perturbation gives
\begin{equation}
 \frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}(C_j\wedge M)
 \xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}(C\wedge M)}{2\tau}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}
\end{equation}
To remove the truncation, put
\[
 D_M(\mathbf x):=
 \sum_{\text{letters }\ell}C(\ell)\mathbf1_{\{C(\ell)>M\}}
 \mathbf x^{\mathbf A(\ell)}.
\]
This series is analytic in a neighborhood of \(\mathbf z\).  Pointing one
letter in a free word gives the exact coefficient identity
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
 =\frac{[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
  D_M(\mathbf x)(1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-2}}
 {[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
  (1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-1}}.
\]
The corresponding smooth-point expansions, or equivalently differentiation
of the analytic perturbation
\(A_{\mathcal P}+sD_M\) at \(s=0\), yield
\[
 \frac1N\mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}
 C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}[C\mathbf1_{\{C>M\}}]}{2\tau}.
\]
First let \(N\to\infty\), then \(M\to\infty\), and use Markov's
inequality together with \eqref{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}.  This
proves the cost limit in \eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}; the
velocity limit follows from
\(N^{-1}\log q_{\mathbf n_N}\to\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i\).

Under \eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}, the free law gives
\[
 \frac{T_N}{m_N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}
 \frac{\alpha}{v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}}<1.
\]
Thus \(\Pr\{T_N\le m_N-1\}\to1\).  By
\eqref{eq:prime-support-window-interface}, the finite-window law on generator
words is obtained from the uniform free-word law by the weight
\(K_{m_N}(T_N)\).  Since this weight is bounded by four and equals four on
an event of probability tending to one, its normalizing constant tends to
four and the two laws converge in total variation.  This proves
\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-count} and
\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}.

On compact subsets of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\), the saddle remains in a
compact subset of \(\prod_i(0,p_i^{-1})\), the transverse covariance stays
uniformly nondegenerate, and the fixed-denominator bound supplies a common
summable majorant for the cost tails.  The smooth-point expansions and all
truncation estimates above are therefore uniform there.
\end{proof}

% The former directional quenched theorem is withdrawn: its proof required a

Write
\[
 \mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}:=
 \{\boldsymbol\rho\in(0,\infty)^d:
   \rho_1+\cdots+\rho_d=1\}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Directional quenched law on finite prime support]
\label{thm:prime-support-directional-quenched}
Retain the notation of \Cref{prop:prime-support-interface}, and fix
\(\boldsymbol\rho\in\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\).  Put
\[
 g_i(z):=\frac{1-z}{1-p_i z},
 \qquad
 h_i(z):=\frac{z g_i'(z)}{g_i(z)}
 =\frac{(p_i-1)z}{(1-z)(1-p_i z)}.
\]
There are unique \(\tau>0\) and
\(\mathbf z=\mathbf z(\boldsymbol\rho)\in
\prod_i(0,p_i^{-1})\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \prod_{i=1}^d g_i(z_i)=2,
 \qquad h_i(z_i)=\tau\rho_i\quad(1\le i\le d).
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}
\end{equation}
More explicitly, \(z_i=\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i)\), where
\begin{equation}
 \zeta_i(x)=
 \frac{(p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x-
  \sqrt{((p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x)^2-4p_i x^2}}
 {2p_i x}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}
\end{equation}
The point \(\mathbf z\) is the unique point of
\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\) in the closed polydisc
\(\{|w_i|\le z_i\}\).

Give every letter \((\mathbf a,h/q_{\mathbf a})\) the probability
\begin{equation}
 \Pr_{\mathbf z}\{(\mathbf A,C)=
  (\mathbf a,c(h/q_{\mathbf a}))\}=\mathbf z^{\mathbf a}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law}
\end{equation}
This is a probability law, and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=2\tau\boldsymbol\rho,
 \qquad m_C(\boldsymbol\rho):=\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}C<\infty.
\]
Define its directional velocity by
\begin{equation}
 v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}:=
 \frac{2\tau\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i}{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-velocity}
\end{equation}

Let \(\mathbf n_N=N\boldsymbol\rho+O(1)\in\mathbb N^d\), and let
\(W_N\) be uniform among the nonempty free generator words of total exponent
\(\mathbf n_N\).  If \(R_N\) is its number of letters and \(T_N\) its
total cost, then
\begin{equation}
 \frac{R_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac1{2\tau},
 \qquad
 \frac{T_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}{2\tau},
 \qquad
 \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{T_N}
 \xrightarrow{\Pr}v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}
\end{equation}

Finally, let \(m_N\to\infty\) be integers such that
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{m_N}\longrightarrow
 \alpha\in[0,v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}).
 \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}
\end{equation}
Then the exact level
\(\{x\in X_{m_N}:d_{m_N}(x)=q_{\mathbf n_N}\}\) is nonempty for all
sufficiently large \(N\),
\begin{equation}
 C_{m_N}(q_{\mathbf n_N})
 \sim4\card{\{\text{free words of exponent }\mathbf n_N\}},
 \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-count}
\end{equation}
and, under the uniform law on this level,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{L(g_{m_N})}{m_N}
 \xrightarrow{\Pr}
 \frac{\alpha}{v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}
\end{equation}
The free-word convergences are uniform when \(\boldsymbol\rho\) ranges over a
compact subset of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\) and
\(\|\mathbf n_N-N\boldsymbol\rho\|\) is bounded.  The finite-window
conclusions are uniform under the additional requirement that the budget
ratio remain bounded away from one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each \(h_i\) is strictly increasing from zero to infinity on
\((0,p_i^{-1})\).  Solving the resulting quadratic gives
\eqref{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}.  Hence
\(\prod_i g_i(\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i))\) increases continuously from one to
infinity, which proves existence and uniqueness in
\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}.  Since
\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1\),
\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law} has total mass one, and
Euler differentiation gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}A_i
 =z_i\partial_{z_i}A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)
 =2h_i(z_i)=2\tau\rho_i.
\]

We verify the strict-minimality and lattice hypotheses needed below.  If
\(|w_i|\le z_i\) and \(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\), coefficient
positivity gives
\[
 1\le A_{\mathcal P}(|\mathbf w|,1)
 \le A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1.
\]
The support contains every \(\mathbf e_i\), so equality in the second
inequality forces \(|w_i|=z_i\) for every \(i\).  Equality in the triangle
inequality then forces all supported monomials to have phase one; applying
this to the \(\mathbf e_i\) gives \(w_i=z_i\).  The same support contains
\(2\mathbf e_i\), so its difference lattice is \(\mathbb Z^d\).  Finally,
the covariance matrix of \(\mathbf A\) is positive definite: if
\(\mathbf t\cdot\mathbf A\) were constant almost surely, comparison of
\(\mathbf e_i\) and \(2\mathbf e_i\) would give \(t_i=0\) for every
\(i\).

The fixed-denominator mean estimate quoted in the proof of
\Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{1\le h<q\\(h,q)=1}}c(h/q)
 =O(q(1+\log q)^2).
\]
Since \(p_i z_i<1\), summation over exponent vectors proves
\(m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)<\infty\).

We now apply the smooth strictly minimal point expansion of
Pemantle--Wilson \cite{PemantleWilson2002}; the preceding paragraph verifies
its nonperiodicity, strict minimality, and nondegenerate transverse Hessian
for the present rational function.  Marking each letter by \(e^s\) and
using the expansion uniformly for small complex \(s\) gives the usual
analytic quasi-powers estimate.  The critical number of letters is determined
by
\[
 r_N\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=N\boldsymbol\rho,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad r_N=\frac{N}{2\tau}.
\]
It follows that \(R_N/N\to1/(2\tau)\) in probability.

For \(M>0\), mark instead the bounded cost \(C\wedge M\).  The same analytic
perturbation gives
\begin{equation}
 \frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}(C_j\wedge M)
 \xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}(C\wedge M)}{2\tau}.
 \label{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}
\end{equation}
To remove the truncation, put
\[
 D_M(\mathbf x):=
 \sum_{\text{letters }\ell}C(\ell)\mathbf1_{\{C(\ell)>M\}}
 \mathbf x^{\mathbf A(\ell)}.
\]
This series is analytic in a neighborhood of \(\mathbf z\).  Pointing one
letter in a free word gives the exact coefficient identity
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
 =\frac{[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
  D_M(\mathbf x)(1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-2}}
 {[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
  (1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-1}}.
\]
The corresponding smooth-point expansions, or equivalently differentiation
of the analytic perturbation
\(A_{\mathcal P}+sD_M\) at \(s=0\), yield
\[
 \frac1N\mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}
 C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}[C\mathbf1_{\{C>M\}}]}{2\tau}.
\]
First let \(N\to\infty\), then \(M\to\infty\), and use Markov's
inequality together with \eqref{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}.  This
proves the cost limit in \eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}; the
velocity limit follows from
\(N^{-1}\log q_{\mathbf n_N}\to\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i\).

Under \eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}, the free law gives
\[
 \frac{T_N}{m_N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}
 \frac{\alpha}{v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}}<1.
\]
Thus \(\Pr\{T_N\le m_N-1\}\to1\).  By
\eqref{eq:prime-support-window-interface}, the finite-window law on generator
words is obtained from the uniform free-word law by the weight
\(K_{m_N}(T_N)\).  Since this weight is bounded by four and equals four on
an event of probability tending to one, its normalizing constant tends to
four and the two laws converge in total variation.  This proves
\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-count} and
\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}.

On compact subsets of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\), the saddle remains in a
compact subset of \(\prod_i(0,p_i^{-1})\), the transverse covariance stays
uniformly nondegenerate, and the fixed-denominator bound supplies a common
summable majorant for the cost tails.  The smooth-point expansions and all
truncation estimates above are therefore uniform there.
\end{proof}

 \begin{abstract}
 Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by

+pressure is the affine normalization
+\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the
+golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\)
+spectrum, while Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and
+its negative first-order phase transition.  We record the exact dictionary
+and recover those results in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  The arithmetic
+refinements identify the critical parameter by
 \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\).  At criticality

+\begin{remark}[Scope of the analytic compact-operator observation]
+\label{rem:compact-operator-scope}
+The frozen interval and \(P(0)=\log\varphi\) exclude only a single
+operator-norm analytic family of compact operators on one fixed Banach space
+whose pressure eigenvalue stays positive, algebraically simple, isolated, and
+locally uniformly separated from the rest of the spectrum across the whole
+real axis.  Analytic perturbation theory would make its logarithm analytic,
+contradicting the frozen interval.  This observation does not exclude
+parameter-dependent spaces, noncompact or countable-state transfer operators,
+families that lose their spectral gap at the critical point, or representations
+defined separately in the two phases.  It is not used below.
+\end{remark}

The following pressure statement is retained because its renewal
normalization is used below.  Its existence, implicit branch, frozen phase,
and nondifferentiable critical point recover the golden-ratio
Bernoulli-convolution results of Feng--Olivier and Feng
\cite{FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}; they are not claimed as new.

\begin{proposition}[Recovery of the Bernoulli-convolution pressure]
\label{thm:exact-negative-pressure}
\label{thm:all-real-pressure}
For every \(s\in\mathbb R\), the radius of convergence of \(B_s\) is
\begin{equation}
 R_B(s)=\exp\{-\mathfrak P(s/2)/2\}.
 \label{eq:Bs-radius}
\end{equation}
Thus \(R_B(s)<1\) for \(s<2\), and \(R_B(s)=1\) for \(s\ge2\).
The nonnegative real roots of \(B_s(r)=1\) are classified as follows:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
s<\sigma_0 & \text{a unique root }r_s\in(0,R_B(s)),\\
s=\sigma_0 & \text{the unique root }r_s=1=R_B(s),\\
s>\sigma_0 & \text{no root in }[0,R_B(s)].
\end{array}
\]
The pressure exists for every real tilt and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 P(-s):=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log S_{-s}(m)
 =\begin{cases}
   -\log r_s,&s<\sigma_0,\\
   0,&s\ge\sigma_0.
  \end{cases}
 \label{eq:all-real-pressure}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, for \(t>-\sigma_0\), \(P(t)>0\) is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{q=2}^{\infty}
 \sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 q^t e^{-P(t)c(p/q)}=1,
 \label{eq:exact-negative-pressure}
\end{equation}
whereas \(P(t)=0\) for \(t\le-\sigma_0\).  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \{t\in\mathbb R:P(t)>0\}=(-\sigma_0,\infty).
 \label{eq:exact-zero-pressure-set}
\end{equation}

The restriction of \(P\) to \((-\sigma_0,\infty)\) is real analytic and
strictly convex.  At \(t_c=-\sigma_0\), it has the finite one-sided
derivatives
\begin{equation}
 P'_-(t_c)=0,
 \qquad
 P'_+(t_c)=
 \frac{\displaystyle
  \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
       q^{-\sigma_0}\log q}
 {\displaystyle
  \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
       c(p/q)q^{-\sigma_0}}>0.
 \label{eq:critical-pressure-slopes}
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(P\) is not differentiable at the freezing point.
\end{theorem}

parameterization gives
\[
 a_d(s)=\sum_{\substack{0<p<q,\ (p,q)=1\\d(p/q)=d}}q^{-s}.
\]

 \begin{abstract}
 Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli

-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative

  768: \begin{theorem}[Full large deviations across the freezing corner]
  769: \label{thm:full-fiber-ldp}
  770: Let \(\mathbf X_m\) be uniformly distributed on \(X_m\), and set
  771: \[
  772:  \begin{gathered}
  773:  y_m(x):=\frac1m\log d_m(x),\qquad
  774:  Y_m:=y_m(\mathbf X_m),\\
  775:  t_c:=-\sigma_0,\qquad v_c:=P'_+(t_c),
  776:  \qquad \alpha_+:=\frac12\log\varphi.
  777:  \end{gathered}
  778: \]
  779: Then \((Y_m)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle with speed \(m\)
  780: and good rate function
  781: \begin{equation}
  782:  I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}
  783:  \{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
  784:  \label{eq:full-fiber-ldp-rate}
  785: \end{equation}
  786: Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\).  On the coexistence interval,
  787: \begin{equation}
  788:  I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
  789:  \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
  790:  \label{eq:frozen-affine-rate}
  791: \end{equation}
  792: More precisely, for every \(0<\alpha<v_c\),
  793: \begin{equation}
  794:  \begin{aligned}
  795:  &\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}
  796:  \frac1m\log\Pr\{|Y_m-\alpha|<\varepsilon\}\\
  797:  &\quad=
  798:  \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{m\to\infty}
  799:  \frac1m\log\Pr\{|Y_m-\alpha|<\varepsilon\}\\
  800:  &\quad=-\bigl(\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\bigr).
  801:  \end{aligned}
  802:  \label{eq:frozen-local-large-deviation}
  803: \end{equation}
  804: \end{theorem}
  805: 
  806: \begin{proof}
  807: For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), write
  808: \[
  809:  A_m(\alpha,\varepsilon)
  810:  :=\card{\left\{x\in X_m:
  811:  \left|m^{-1}\log d_m(x)-\alpha\right|<\varepsilon\right\}}.
  812: \]
  813: We first establish the lower bound at the nonexposed slopes.  Fix
  814: \(t>t_c\), put \(v=P'(t)>v_c\), and define the tilted law on \(X_n\) by
  815: \[
  816:  \nu_{n,t}(x):=\frac{d_n(x)^t}{S_t(n)}.
  817: \]
  818: For sufficiently small \(s>0\), the exponential Markov inequality and
  819: \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} give
  820: \[
  821:  \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n
  822:  \log\nu_{n,t}\{y_n\ge v+\delta\}
  823:  \le P(t+s)-P(t)-s(v+\delta)<0.
  824: \]
  825: The corresponding estimate with \(s<0\) gives the same conclusion for
  826: \(y_n\le v-\delta\).  Consequently,
  827: \[
  828:  \sum_{\substack{x\in X_n\\|y_n(x)-v|<\delta}}d_n(x)^t
  829:  =\exp\{n(P(t)+o(1))\}.
  830: \]
  831: Every summand on the left is at most
  832: \(\exp\{n(tv+|t|\delta)\}\), and hence
  833: \begin{equation}
  834:  \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log A_n(v,\delta)
  835:  \ge P(t)-tv-|t|\delta.
  836:  \label{eq:exposed-source-count}
  837: \end{equation}
  838: 
  839: We now transfer these source states to a larger layer without changing their
  840: multiplicities.  The proof of \Cref{thm:fiber-partition-interval} gives the
  841: explicit bijection
  842: \[
  843:  \chi_n(x)=
  844:  \begin{cases}
  845:   F_{n+2}+V_n(x),&0\le V_n(x)\le F_{n+1}-2,\\
  846:   V_n(x),&F_{n+1}-1\le V_n(x)<F_{n+2},
  847:  \end{cases}
  848: \]
  849: from \(X_n\) onto the integer points of
  850: \(\mathcal I_n\sqcup\mathcal I_{n+1}\), with
  851: \(d_n(x)=R(\chi_n(x))\).  Take
  852: \(\delta<v/2\), so their multiplicities exceed two for all sufficiently
  853: large \(n\).  The uniform layer-count lemma shows that each Weinstein
  854: generating orbit supplies at most four source states to these two layers.
  855: The specialized formulas in the proof of
  856: \Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal} give
  857: \[
  858:  L([a]g)=L(g)+2a,\qquad
  859:  L([a]\tau g)=L(g)+1+2a,
  860: \]
  861: and the two sigma branches increase these lengths by one.  Hence every orbit
  862: meeting \(\mathcal I_n\sqcup\mathcal I_{n+1}\) has generator length at most
  863: \(n+1\).
  864: Keeping the generating number of every orbit which occurs therefore gives a
  865: set \(\mathcal G_n\) such that
  866: \begin{equation}
  867:  \card{\mathcal G_n}\ge\frac14 A_n(v,\delta),
  868:  \qquad L(g)\le n+1\quad(g\in\mathcal G_n),
  869:  \label{eq:source-generating-orbits}
  870: \end{equation}
  871: and \(n^{-1}\log R(g)\in(v-\delta,v+\delta)\), since the orbit action
  872: preserves \(R\).  Distinct elements of
  873: \(\mathcal G_n\) generate disjoint orbits.
  874: 
  875: Fix \(0<\alpha<v_c\), set \(\rho=\alpha/v\), and let
  876: \(n_m=\lfloor\rho m\rfloor\).  For sufficiently large \(m\), every
  877: \(g\in\mathcal G_{n_m}\) has \(L(g)<m\).  The generator formulas in the
  878: proof of \Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal} permit the parity-free
  879: definition
  880: \[
  881:  z_m(g):=
  882:  \begin{cases}
  883:  [a]g,&m-L(g)=2a,\\
  884:  [a]\tau g,&m-L(g)=2a+1.
  885:  \end{cases}
  886: \]
  887: They give \(L(z_m(g))=m\) and \(R(z_m(g))=R(g)>1\).  Thus
  888: \(z_m(g)\in\mathcal I_m\), and \(\chi_m^{-1}\) turns these into distinct
  889: states of \(X_m\).  Moreover,
  890: \[
  891:  \left|m^{-1}\log R(z_m(g))-\alpha\right|
  892:  \le \frac{n_m}{m}\delta+\frac vm.
  893: \]
  894: Combining this injection with
  895: \eqref{eq:exposed-source-count}--\eqref{eq:source-generating-orbits} yields,
  896: for every \(\varepsilon>\rho\delta\),
  897: \begin{equation}
  898:  \liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log A_m(\alpha,\varepsilon)
  899:  \ge \rho\bigl(P(t)-tv-|t|\delta\bigr).
  900:  \label{eq:orbit-filling-lower-bound}
  901: \end{equation}
  902: First let \(\delta\downarrow0\), and then let \(t\downarrow t_c\).  Since
  903: \(P(t)\to0\), \(P'(t)=v\to v_c\), and
  904: \[
  905:  \rho(P(t)-tv)=\alpha\left(\frac{P(t)}v-t\right)
  906:  \longrightarrow-t_c\alpha=\sigma_0\alpha,
  907: \]
  908: we obtain
  909: \begin{equation}
  910:  \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}
  911:  \frac1m\log A_m(\alpha,\varepsilon)
  912:  \ge\sigma_0\alpha.
  913:  \label{eq:frozen-count-lower}
  914: \end{equation}
  915: 
  916: The matching upper bound uses the critical pressure directly.  On the set
  917: counted by \(A_m(\alpha,\varepsilon)\),
  918: \(d_m(x)^{-\sigma_0}\ge
  919: \exp\{-\sigma_0m(\alpha+\varepsilon)\}\).  Therefore
  920: \[
  921:  A_m(\alpha,\varepsilon)
  922:  e^{-\sigma_0m(\alpha+\varepsilon)}
  923:  \le S_{-\sigma_0}(m)=e^{o(m)},
  924: \]
  925: which, together with \eqref{eq:frozen-count-lower}, proves the corresponding
  926: counting limit.  Since \(\card{X_m}=F_{m+2}\) and
  927: \(m^{-1}\log F_{m+2}\to\log\varphi\), this is
  928: \eqref{eq:frozen-local-large-deviation}.
  929: 
  930: We next identify the convex dual.  If \(0\le\alpha\le v_c\), then
  931: \(P(t)=0\) for \(t\le t_c\), while convexity and the right derivative at
  932: \(t_c\) give \(P(t)\ge v_c(t-t_c)\) for \(t\ge t_c\).  It follows that
  933: \(t\alpha-P(t)\le t_c\alpha\) for every \(t\), with equality at
  934: \(t=t_c\), proving \eqref{eq:frozen-affine-rate}.
  935: 
  936: The exact maximum theorem gives
  937: \[
  938:  \max_{x\in X_m}m^{-1}\log d_m(x)\longrightarrow\alpha_+.
  939: \]
  940: For \(t>0\), the bounds
  941: \(D_m^t\le S_t(m)\le F_{m+2}D_m^t\) imply
  942: \[
  943:  \alpha_+\le\frac{P(t)}t
  944:  \le\alpha_++\frac{\log\varphi}{t}.
  945: \]
  946: By convexity, (P') is increasing and therefore has a limit in
  947: \((0,+\infty]\).  The identity
  948: \[
  949:  \frac{P(t)}t=\frac{P(0)}t+\frac1t\int_0^t P'(u)\,du
  950: \]
  951: and Ces\`aro convergence show that this limit is \(\alpha_+\).  Thus
  952: \(P'(t)\uparrow\alpha_+\) as \(t\to\infty\).  Strict convexity and
  953: analyticity on \((t_c,\infty)\) now show that every
  954: \(\alpha\in(v_c,\alpha_+)\) is exposed by a unique \(t>t_c\).  The tilted
  955: estimate above with \(n=m\) supplies
  956: \begin{equation}
  957:  \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}
  958:  \frac1m\log\Pr\{|Y_m-\alpha|<\varepsilon\}
  959:  \ge P(t)-t\alpha-\log\varphi=-I(\alpha).
  960:  \label{eq:exposed-local-large-deviation}
  961: \end{equation}
  962: 
  963: Finally, the logarithmic moment generating functions under the uniform law
  964: converge on all of \(\mathbb R\) to
  965: \[
  966:  \Lambda(t)=P(t)-\log\varphi.
  967: \]
  968: The variables are eventually supported in a fixed compact interval, so they
  969: are exponentially tight.  The G\"artner--Ellis upper bound
  970: \cite[Theorem~2.3.6(a)]{DemboZeitouni2010} therefore gives the
  971: large-deviation upper bound for all closed sets.
  972: 
  973: It remains to justify the effective domain and endpoint lower bounds.  If
  974: \(\alpha<0\), letting \(t\to-\infty\) in
  975: \eqref{eq:full-fiber-ldp-rate} and using \(P(t)=0\) gives
  976: \(I(\alpha)=+\infty\).  If \(\alpha>\alpha_+\), the limit
  977: \(P(t)/t\to\alpha_+\) gives the same conclusion as \(t\to\infty\).
  978: Conversely, if \(0\le\alpha\le\alpha_+\), then
  979: \(t\alpha-P(t)\) is bounded above on \(( -\infty,t_c]\), on the compact
  980: interval \([t_c,0]\), and on \([0,\infty)\), where
  981: \(P(t)\ge t\alpha_+\).  Thus the effective domain is exactly
  982: \([0,\alpha_+]\).  The rate is a lower-semicontinuous convex function, and
  983: its finiteness on this closed interval implies continuity relative to the
  984: interval, including at the endpoints.
  985: 
  986: The local lower bounds already proved cover the coexistence and exposed
  987: parts of \((0,\alpha_+)\), and points from either side approximate \(v_c\).
  988: At \(0\), the two singleton fibers give the lower bound directly.  At
  989: \(\alpha_+\), continuity of \(I\) and exposed points approaching from below
  990: supply the lower bound for every open neighborhood.  Hence the lower bound
  991: holds for every open set.  The effective domain is compact and \(I\) is
  992: lower semicontinuous, so \(I\) is good and the full large deviation principle
  993: follows.
  994: \end{proof}

 \begin{abstract}

-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by

+\begin{remark}[Scope of the analytic compact-operator observation]
+\label{rem:compact-operator-scope}

 \begin{abstract}
 Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by

+representation frequencies are the same subset-sum coefficients after the
+shift from their convention \(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\).  Their normalized
+frequencies approximate the Erd\H{o}s measure.  Consequently the layer moment
+pressure is the affine normalization
+\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the
+golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\)
+spectrum, while Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and
+its negative first-order phase transition.  We record the exact dictionary
+and recover those results in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  The arithmetic
+refinements identify the critical parameter by
 \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\).  At criticality
 the one-layer partition sum is asymptotic to \(2m/\mu_C\), and its Gibbs law

+\label{rem:compact-operator-scope}

+parameter-dependent spaces, noncompact or countable-state transfer operators,

- \qquad h_i(z_i)=\tau\rho_i\quad(1\le i\le d).
- \label{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}
-\end{equation}
-More explicitly, \(z_i=\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i)\), where
-\begin{equation}
- \zeta_i(x)=
- \frac{(p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x-
-  \sqrt{((p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x)^2-4p_i x^2}}
- {2p_i x}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}
-\end{equation}
-The point \(\mathbf z\) is the unique point of
-\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\) in the closed polydisc
-\(\{|w_i|\le z_i\}\).
-
-Give every letter \((\mathbf a,h/q_{\mathbf a})\) the probability
-\begin{equation}
- \Pr_{\mathbf z}\{(\mathbf A,C)=
-  (\mathbf a,c(h/q_{\mathbf a}))\}=\mathbf z^{\mathbf a}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law}
-\end{equation}
-This is a probability law, and
-\[
- \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=2\tau\boldsymbol\rho,
- \qquad m_C(\boldsymbol\rho):=\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}C<\infty.
-\]
-Define its directional velocity by
-\begin{equation}
- v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}:=
- \frac{2\tau\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i}{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-directional-velocity}
-\end{equation}
-
-Let \(\mathbf n_N=N\boldsymbol\rho+O(1)\in\mathbb N^d\), and let
-\(W_N\) be uniform among the nonempty free generator words of total exponent
-\(\mathbf n_N\).  If \(R_N\) is its number of letters and \(T_N\) its
-total cost, then
-\begin{equation}
- \frac{R_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac1{2\tau},
- \qquad
- \frac{T_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}{2\tau},
- \qquad
- \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{T_N}
- \xrightarrow{\Pr}v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}
-\end{equation}
-
-Finally, let \(m_N\to\infty\) be integers such that
-\begin{equation}
- \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{m_N}\longrightarrow
- \alpha\in[0,v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}).
- \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}
-\end{equation}
-Then the exact level
-\(\{x\in X_{m_N}:d_{m_N}(x)=q_{\mathbf n_N}\}\) is nonempty for all
-sufficiently large \(N\),
-\begin{equation}
- C_{m_N}(q_{\mathbf n_N})
- \sim4\card{\{\text{free words of exponent }\mathbf n_N\}},
- \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-count}
-\end{equation}
-and, under the uniform law on this level,
-\begin{equation}
- \frac{L(g_{m_N})}{m_N}
- \xrightarrow{\Pr}
- \frac{\alpha}{v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}
-\end{equation}
-The free-word convergences are uniform when \(\boldsymbol\rho\) ranges over a
-compact subset of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\) and
-\(\|\mathbf n_N-N\boldsymbol\rho\|\) is bounded.  The finite-window
-conclusions are uniform under the additional requirement that the budget
-ratio remain bounded away from one.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Each \(h_i\) is strictly increasing from zero to infinity on
-\((0,p_i^{-1})\).  Solving the resulting quadratic gives
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}.  Hence
-\(\prod_i g_i(\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i))\) increases continuously from one to
-infinity, which proves existence and uniqueness in
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}.  Since
-\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1\),
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law} has total mass one, and
-Euler differentiation gives
-\[
- \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}A_i
- =z_i\partial_{z_i}A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)
- =2h_i(z_i)=2\tau\rho_i.
-\]
-
-We verify the strict-minimality and lattice hypotheses needed below.  If
-\(|w_i|\le z_i\) and \(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\), coefficient
-positivity gives
-\[
- 1\le A_{\mathcal P}(|\mathbf w|,1)
- \le A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1.
-\]
-The support contains every \(\mathbf e_i\), so equality in the second
-inequality forces \(|w_i|=z_i\) for every \(i\).  Equality in the triangle
-inequality then forces all supported monomials to have phase one; applying
-this to the \(\mathbf e_i\) gives \(w_i=z_i\).  The same support contains
-\(2\mathbf e_i\), so its difference lattice is \(\mathbb Z^d\).  Finally,
-the covariance matrix of \(\mathbf A\) is positive definite: if
-\(\mathbf t\cdot\mathbf A\) were constant almost surely, comparison of
-\(\mathbf e_i\) and \(2\mathbf e_i\) would give \(t_i=0\) for every
-\(i\).
-
-The fixed-denominator mean estimate quoted in the proof of
-\Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
-\[
- \sum_{\substack{1\le h<q\\(h,q)=1}}c(h/q)
- =O(q(1+\log q)^2).
-\]
-Since \(p_i z_i<1\), summation over exponent vectors proves
-\(m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)<\infty\).
-
-We now apply the smooth strictly minimal point expansion of
-Pemantle--Wilson \cite{PemantleWilson2002}; the preceding paragraph verifies
-its nonperiodicity, strict minimality, and nondegenerate transverse Hessian
-for the present rational function.  Marking each letter by \(e^s\) and
-using the expansion uniformly for small complex \(s\) gives the usual
-analytic quasi-powers estimate.  The critical number of letters is determined
-by
-\[
- r_N\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=N\boldsymbol\rho,
- \qquad\text{hence}\qquad r_N=\frac{N}{2\tau}.
-\]
-It follows that \(R_N/N\to1/(2\tau)\) in probability.
-
-For \(M>0\), mark instead the bounded cost \(C\wedge M\).  The same analytic
-perturbation gives
-\begin{equation}
- \frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}(C_j\wedge M)
- \xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}(C\wedge M)}{2\tau}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}
-\end{equation}
-To remove the truncation, put
-\[
- D_M(\mathbf x):=
- \sum_{\text{letters }\ell}C(\ell)\mathbf1_{\{C(\ell)>M\}}
- \mathbf x^{\mathbf A(\ell)}.
-\]
-This series is analytic in a neighborhood of \(\mathbf z\).  Pointing one
-letter in a free word gives the exact coefficient identity
-\[
- \mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
- =\frac{[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
-  D_M(\mathbf x)(1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-2}}
- {[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
-  (1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-1}}.
-\]
-The corresponding smooth-point expansions, or equivalently differentiation
-of the analytic perturbation
-\(A_{\mathcal P}+sD_M\) at \(s=0\), yield
-\[
- \frac1N\mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}
- C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
- \longrightarrow
- \frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}[C\mathbf1_{\{C>M\}}]}{2\tau}.
-\]
-First let \(N\to\infty\), then \(M\to\infty\), and use Markov's
-inequality together with \eqref{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}.  This
-proves the cost limit in \eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}; the
-velocity limit follows from
-\(N^{-1}\log q_{\mathbf n_N}\to\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i\).
-
-Under \eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}, the free law gives
-\[
- \frac{T_N}{m_N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}
- \frac{\alpha}{v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}}<1.
-\]
-Thus \(\Pr\{T_N\le m_N-1\}\to1\).  By
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-window-interface}, the finite-window law on generator
-words is obtained from the uniform free-word law by the weight
-\(K_{m_N}(T_N)\).  Since this weight is bounded by four and equals four on
-an event of probability tending to one, its normalizing constant tends to
-four and the two laws converge in total variation.  This proves
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-count} and
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}.
-
-On compact subsets of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\), the saddle remains in a
-compact subset of \(\prod_i(0,p_i^{-1})\), the transverse covariance stays
-uniformly nondegenerate, and the fixed-denominator bound supplies a common
-summable majorant for the cost tails.  The smooth-point expansions and all
-truncation estimates above are therefore uniform there.
-\end{proof}
-\fi

 \begin{abstract}
 Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by
+numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Sidorov--Vershik's finite
+representation frequencies are the same subset-sum coefficients after the
+shift from their convention \(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\).  Their normalized
+frequencies approximate the Erd\H{o}s measure.  Consequently the layer moment
+pressure is the affine normalization
+\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the
+golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\)
+spectrum, while Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and
+its negative first-order phase transition.  We record the exact dictionary
+and recover those results in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  The arithmetic
+refinements identify the critical parameter by
 \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\).  At criticality
 the one-layer partition sum is asymptotic to \(2m/\mu_C\), and its Gibbs law

-this to the \(\mathbf e_i\) gives \(w_i=z_i\).  The same support contains

-the covariance matrix of \(\mathbf A\) is positive definite: if

  278: \begin{theorem}[Joint generation-cost and multiplicity large deviations]
  279: \label{thm:joint-cost-reward-ldp}
  280: The vectors \((B_m^R,Y_m^R)\) satisfy a full large deviation principle on
  281: \(\mathbb R^2\) with speed \(m\).  Their limiting logarithmic moment generating
  282: function is
  283: \begin{equation}
  284:  \Lambda(a,t)=\max\{0,a+P(t)\}-\log\varphi
  285:  \qquad(a,t\in\mathbb R).
  286:  \label{eq:joint-cost-reward-log-mgf}
  287: \end{equation}
  288: The good rate function is
  289: \begin{equation}
  290:  J(\beta,\alpha)=
  291:  \begin{cases}
  292:   (1-\beta)\log\varphi+\beta I(\alpha/\beta),
  293:    &0<\beta\le1,\quad 0\le\alpha\le\beta\alpha_+,\\
  294:   \log\varphi,&(\beta,\alpha)=(0,0),\\
  295:   +\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
  296:  \end{cases}
  297:  \label{eq:joint-cost-reward-rate}
  298: \end{equation}
  299: In particular, the rate surface has the affine face
  300: \begin{equation}
  301:  J(\beta,\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
  302:  \qquad(0\le\beta\le1,\ 0\le\alpha\le\beta v_c).
  303:  \label{eq:joint-cost-reward-flat-face}
  304: \end{equation}
  305: \end{theorem}
  306: 
  307: \begin{proof}
  308: Let \(\mathcal W_j\) be the set of nonempty free generator words of total
  309: cost \(j\), and write \(Q(w)\) for the product of the denominators of the
  310: letters of \(w\).  By \eqref{eq:generator-weight-length},
  311: \begin{equation}
  312:  u_j(-t)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W_j}Q(w)^t.
  313:  \label{eq:fixed-cost-word-partition}
  314: \end{equation}
  315: The convention \(\ell_m^R=0\) at multiplicities at most two changes only a
  316: bounded number of states.  The one-layer orbit weights in
  317: \eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} therefore give, up to a term bounded
  318: for each fixed \((a,t)\),
  319: \begin{equation}
  320:  \sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}e^{a\ell_m^R(n)}R(n)^t
  321:  =2\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}e^{aj}u_j(-t)+e^{am}u_m(-t)+O_{a,t}(1).
  322:  \label{eq:joint-cost-reward-renewal}
  323: \end{equation}
  324: More precisely, the bounded correction removes the level-two generator orbit
  325: from its positive cost and records it at cost zero; the level-one endpoint is
  326: already a cost-zero term.
  327: 
  328: The proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} established
  329: \(\lim_{j\to\infty}j^{-1}\log u_j(-t)=P(t)\), and \(u_j(-t)>0\) for every
  330: \(j\ge8\).  Applying these facts to the partial sum in
  331: \eqref{eq:joint-cost-reward-renewal}, while retaining the level-one endpoint,
  332: gives
  333: \[
  334:  \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log
  335:  \sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}e^{a\ell_m^R(n)}R(n)^t
  336:  =\max\{0,a+P(t)\}.
  337: \]
  338: Since \(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\), this proves
  339: \eqref{eq:joint-cost-reward-log-mgf}.
  340: 
  341: We next compute its convex dual.  For fixed \(t\),
  342: \[
  343:  \sup_{a\in\mathbb R}\{a\beta-\max(0,a+P(t))\}
  344:  =\begin{cases}
  345:    -\beta P(t),&0\le\beta\le1,\\
  346:    +\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
  347:   \end{cases}
  348: \]
  349: For \(0<\beta\le1\), subsequent optimization over \(t\) gives
  350: \[
  351:  \log\varphi+\beta\sup_t\{t\alpha/\beta-P(t)\}
  352:  =(1-\beta)\log\varphi+\beta I(\alpha/\beta).
  353: \]
  354: At \(\beta=0\), the dual is finite only at \(\alpha=0\), where it equals
  355: \(\log\varphi\).  The effective domain of \(I\) from
  356: \Cref{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics} now gives exactly
  357: \eqref{eq:joint-cost-reward-rate}.  The variables are supported in a common
  358: compact set up to a vanishing enlargement: \(0\le B_m^R\le1\), and
  359: \eqref{eq:standard-layer-maximum} bounds \(Y_m^R\).  Thus the
  360: G\"artner--Ellis upper bound applies to every closed set.
  361: 
  362: It remains to prove the lower bound, because the interior points with
  363: \(0<\beta<1\) are not exposed points of \(\Lambda\).  Fix \(t>t_c\) and put
  364: \(v=P'(t)>v_c\).  On \(\mathcal W_j\), use the probability proportional to
  365: \(Q(w)^t\).  For sufficiently small real \(s\),
  366: \eqref{eq:fixed-cost-word-partition} and the fixed-cost pressure limit give
  367: \[
  368:  \limsup_{j\to\infty}\frac1j\log
  369:  \Pr_t\left\{\left|j^{-1}\log Q(w)-v\right|\ge\delta\right\}<0.
  370: \]
  371: This is the same two-sided exponential Markov argument as in
  372: \eqref{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}.  Consequently,
  373: \begin{equation}
  374:  \liminf_{j\to\infty}\frac1j\log
  375:  \card{\{w\in\mathcal W_j:\ |j^{-1}\log Q(w)-v|<\delta\}}
  376:  \ge P(t)-tv-|t|\delta.
  377:  \label{eq:fixed-cost-exposed-source}
  378: \end{equation}
  379: 
  380: Let \(0<\beta\le1\) and suppose first that
  381: \(\alpha/\beta=v>v_c\).  Taking integers \(j_m\) with \(j_m/m\to\beta\),
  382: each word counted in \eqref{eq:fixed-cost-exposed-source} determines at least
  383: one point of \(\mathcal I_m\), because a generator orbit of cost \(j_m\le m\)
  384: meets that layer.  Freeness preserves injectivity.  Hence the local counting
  385: exponent is at least
  386: \(\beta(P(t)-t\alpha/\beta)\), which, after division by \(F_m\), is
  387: \(-J(\beta,\alpha)\).  The same conclusion at \(v_c\) follows by approximation
  388: from \(t\downarrow t_c\).
  389: 
  390: Now let \(0<\alpha\le\beta v_c\).  Keep \(t>t_c\), put \(v=P'(t)\), and choose
  391: integers
  392: \[
  393:  k_m/m\longrightarrow\alpha/v,\qquad j_m/m\longrightarrow\beta.
  394: \]
  395: Then \(r_m:=j_m-k_m\) tends linearly to infinity.  Every integer \(r\ge6\)
  396: is the total cost of at most two letters with logarithmic multiplier
  397: \(O(\log r)\): if \(r\) is odd, use the letter \(1/q\) with
  398: \(q=(r+1)/2\), whose cost is \(2q-1=r\); if \(r\) is even, use \(1/2\) and
  399: \(1/q\) with \(q=(r-2)/2\).  Append this fixed suffix to every source word of
  400: cost \(k_m\) counted in \eqref{eq:fixed-cost-exposed-source}.  The free-monoid
  401: property again gives an injection, the total cost is exactly \(j_m\), and the
  402: added reward is \(o(m)\).  The resulting local counting exponent is at least
  403: \[
  404:  \frac{\alpha}{v}\{P(t)-tv\}.
  405: \]
  406: Letting \(t\downarrow t_c=-\sigma_0\), and using \(P(t)\to0\) and
  407: \(v\downarrow v_c\), gives the exponent \(\sigma_0\alpha\).  For \(\alpha=0\)
  408: the filler word alone gives exponent zero.  After normalization by \(F_m\),
  409: these bounds equal the negative of
  410: \eqref{eq:joint-cost-reward-flat-face}.  The point \((0,0)\) is supplied by
  411: the level-one endpoint.  Finally, points with
  412: \(\alpha=\beta\alpha_+\) follow by approximation from the relative interior;
  413: the finite convex rate in \eqref{eq:joint-cost-reward-rate} is continuous on
  414: its compact effective domain.  This proves the lower bound for every open set
  415: and completes the full LDP.
  416: \end{proof}
  417: 
  418: \begin{remark}[Open second-order critical-cost interface]
  419: \label{rem:critical-cost-tail-open-interface}
  420: The preceding theorem uses only exponential rates and does not identify a
  421: second-order critical renewal term.  Such a result would require, at a
  422: minimum, a uniform mixed-denominator estimate of the form
  423: \[
  424:  \sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
  425:  \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}}
  426:  \sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0}\qquad(x\to\infty)
  427: \]
  428: with \(K_C>0\), including a proof that multiple large partial quotients and
  429: possible lattice oscillations are lower order.  Fixed-denominator estimates
  430: such as \cite{AistleitnerBordaHauke2023} do not by themselves provide the
  431: uniform summation in the critical range \(q\asymp x\).  No such regular
  432: variation statement, and hence no \(m^{3-\sigma_0}\) correction to the
  433: critical partition sum, is asserted here.
  434: \end{remark}

 \begin{abstract}
 Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by
+numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Sidorov--Vershik's finite
+representation frequencies are the same subset-sum coefficients after the
+shift from their convention \(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\).  Their normalized
+frequencies approximate the Erd\H{o}s measure.  Consequently the layer moment
+pressure is the affine normalization
+\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the
+golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\)
+spectrum, while Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and
+its negative first-order phase transition.  We record the exact dictionary
+and recover those results in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  The arithmetic
+refinements identify the critical parameter by
 \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\).  At criticality
 the one-layer partition sum is asymptotic to \(2m/\mu_C\), and its Gibbs law
 converges to a uniform mixture of generating-layer fractions.  Under the
@@ -90,7 +94,7 @@

 \begin{abstract}

-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by
+numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Sidorov--Vershik's finite
+representation frequencies are the same subset-sum coefficients after the

+\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the

+\begin{remark}[Scope of the analytic compact-operator observation]
+\label{rem:compact-operator-scope}
+The frozen interval and \(P(0)=\log\varphi\) exclude only a single
+operator-norm analytic family of compact operators on one fixed Banach space

+defined separately in the two phases.  It is not used below.

 \begin{abstract}

-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by

 \begin{abstract}
 Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
-numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Its layer moment pressure is an
-affine normalization of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
-convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\) spectrum, and
-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
-first-order phase transition.  We give the exact finite-count dictionary and
-recover that pressure in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  Our refinements
-identify its critical parameter arithmetically by
+numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Sidorov--Vershik's finite
+representation frequencies are the same subset-sum coefficients after the
+shift from their convention \(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\).  Their normalized
+frequencies approximate the Erd\H{o}s measure.  Consequently the layer moment
+pressure is the affine normalization
+\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the
+golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\)
+spectrum, while Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and
+its negative first-order phase transition.  We record the exact dictionary
+and recover those results in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  The arithmetic
+refinements identify the critical parameter by
 \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\).  At criticality
 the one-layer partition sum is asymptotic to \(2m/\mu_C\), and its Gibbs law
 converges to a uniform mixture of generating-layer fractions.  Under the
@@ -90,7 +94,7 @@

-\begin{theorem}[Directional quenched law on finite prime support]
-\label{thm:prime-support-directional-quenched}
-Retain the notation of \Cref{prop:prime-support-interface}, and fix
-\(\boldsymbol\rho\in\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\).  Put
-\[
- g_i(z):=\frac{1-z}{1-p_i z},
- \qquad
- h_i(z):=\frac{z g_i'(z)}{g_i(z)}
- =\frac{(p_i-1)z}{(1-z)(1-p_i z)}.
-\]
-There are unique \(\tau>0\) and
-\(\mathbf z=\mathbf z(\boldsymbol\rho)\in
-\prod_i(0,p_i^{-1})\) such that
-\begin{equation}
- \prod_{i=1}^d g_i(z_i)=2,
- \qquad h_i(z_i)=\tau\rho_i\quad(1\le i\le d).
- \label{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}
-\end{equation}
-More explicitly, \(z_i=\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i)\), where
-\begin{equation}
- \zeta_i(x)=
- \frac{(p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x-
-  \sqrt{((p_i-1)+(p_i+1)x)^2-4p_i x^2}}
- {2p_i x}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}
-\end{equation}
-The point \(\mathbf z\) is the unique point of
-\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\) in the closed polydisc
-\(\{|w_i|\le z_i\}\).

-Give every letter \((\mathbf a,h/q_{\mathbf a})\) the probability
-\begin{equation}
- \Pr_{\mathbf z}\{(\mathbf A,C)=
-  (\mathbf a,c(h/q_{\mathbf a}))\}=\mathbf z^{\mathbf a}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law}
-\end{equation}

-\[
- \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=2\tau\boldsymbol\rho,
- \qquad m_C(\boldsymbol\rho):=\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}C<\infty.

-Define its directional velocity by
-\begin{equation}

- \frac{2\tau\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i}{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}.

-\end{equation}

-Let \(\mathbf n_N=N\boldsymbol\rho+O(1)\in\mathbb N^d\), and let
-\(W_N\) be uniform among the nonempty free generator words of total exponent
-\(\mathbf n_N\).  If \(R_N\) is its number of letters and \(T_N\) its
-total cost, then
-\begin{equation}
- \frac{R_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac1{2\tau},
- \qquad
- \frac{T_N}{N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)}{2\tau},
- \qquad
- \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{T_N}
- \xrightarrow{\Pr}v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}
-\end{equation}
-
-Finally, let \(m_N\to\infty\) be integers such that
-\begin{equation}
- \frac{\log q_{\mathbf n_N}}{m_N}\longrightarrow
- \alpha\in[0,v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}).
- \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}
-\end{equation}
-Then the exact level
-\(\{x\in X_{m_N}:d_{m_N}(x)=q_{\mathbf n_N}\}\) is nonempty for all

-\begin{equation}

- \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-count}
-\end{equation}

-\begin{equation}

- \xrightarrow{\Pr}

- \label{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}
-\end{equation}
-The free-word convergences are uniform when \(\boldsymbol\rho\) ranges over a

-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-Each \(h_i\) is strictly increasing from zero to infinity on
-\((0,p_i^{-1})\).  Solving the resulting quadratic gives
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-correct-inverse}.  Hence
-\(\prod_i g_i(\zeta_i(\tau\rho_i))\) increases continuously from one to
-infinity, which proves existence and uniqueness in
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-saddle}.  Since
-\(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1\),
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-letter-law} has total mass one, and
-Euler differentiation gives
-\[
- \mathbb E_{\mathbf z}A_i
- =z_i\partial_{z_i}A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)
- =2h_i(z_i)=2\tau\rho_i.
-\]
-
-We verify the strict-minimality and lattice hypotheses needed below.  If
-\(|w_i|\le z_i\) and \(A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf w,1)=1\), coefficient
-positivity gives
-\[
- 1\le A_{\mathcal P}(|\mathbf w|,1)
- \le A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf z,1)=1.
-\]
-The support contains every \(\mathbf e_i\), so equality in the second
-inequality forces \(|w_i|=z_i\) for every \(i\).  Equality in the triangle
-inequality then forces all supported monomials to have phase one; applying
-this to the \(\mathbf e_i\) gives \(w_i=z_i\).  The same support contains
-\(2\mathbf e_i\), so its difference lattice is \(\mathbb Z^d\).  Finally,
-the covariance matrix of \(\mathbf A\) is positive definite: if
-\(\mathbf t\cdot\mathbf A\) were constant almost surely, comparison of
-\(\mathbf e_i\) and \(2\mathbf e_i\) would give \(t_i=0\) for every
-\(i\).
-
-The fixed-denominator mean estimate quoted in the proof of
-\Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
-\[
- \sum_{\substack{1\le h<q\\(h,q)=1}}c(h/q)
- =O(q(1+\log q)^2).
-\]
-Since \(p_i z_i<1\), summation over exponent vectors proves
-\(m_C(\boldsymbol\rho)<\infty\).
-
-We now apply the smooth strictly minimal point expansion of
-Pemantle--Wilson \cite{PemantleWilson2002}; the preceding paragraph verifies
-its nonperiodicity, strict minimality, and nondegenerate transverse Hessian
-for the present rational function.  Marking each letter by \(e^s\) and
-using the expansion uniformly for small complex \(s\) gives the usual
-analytic quasi-powers estimate.  The critical number of letters is determined
-by
-\[
- r_N\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}\mathbf A=N\boldsymbol\rho,
- \qquad\text{hence}\qquad r_N=\frac{N}{2\tau}.
-\]
-It follows that \(R_N/N\to1/(2\tau)\) in probability.
-
-For \(M>0\), mark instead the bounded cost \(C\wedge M\).  The same analytic
-perturbation gives
-\begin{equation}
- \frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}(C_j\wedge M)
- \xrightarrow{\Pr}\frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}(C\wedge M)}{2\tau}.
- \label{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}
-\end{equation}
-To remove the truncation, put
-\[
- D_M(\mathbf x):=
- \sum_{\text{letters }\ell}C(\ell)\mathbf1_{\{C(\ell)>M\}}
- \mathbf x^{\mathbf A(\ell)}.
-\]
-This series is analytic in a neighborhood of \(\mathbf z\).  Pointing one
-letter in a free word gives the exact coefficient identity
-\[
- \mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
- =\frac{[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
-  D_M(\mathbf x)(1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-2}}
- {[\mathbf x^{\mathbf n_N}]
-  (1-A_{\mathcal P}(\mathbf x,1))^{-1}}.
-\]
-The corresponding smooth-point expansions, or equivalently differentiation
-of the analytic perturbation
-\(A_{\mathcal P}+sD_M\) at \(s=0\), yield
-\[
- \frac1N\mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^{R_N}
- C_j\mathbf1_{\{C_j>M\}}
- \longrightarrow
- \frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf z}[C\mathbf1_{\{C>M\}}]}{2\tau}.
-\]
-First let \(N\to\infty\), then \(M\to\infty\), and use Markov's
-inequality together with \eqref{eq:prime-support-truncated-cost-law}.  This
-proves the cost limit in \eqref{eq:prime-support-directional-free-law}; the
-velocity limit follows from
-\(N^{-1}\log q_{\mathbf n_N}\to\sum_i\rho_i\log p_i\).
-
-Under \eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-budget}, the free law gives
-\[
- \frac{T_N}{m_N}\xrightarrow{\Pr}
- \frac{\alpha}{v_{\mathcal P,\boldsymbol\rho}}<1.
-\]
-Thus \(\Pr\{T_N\le m_N-1\}\to1\).  By
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-window-interface}, the finite-window law on generator
-words is obtained from the uniform free-word law by the weight
-\(K_{m_N}(T_N)\).  Since this weight is bounded by four and equals four on
-an event of probability tending to one, its normalizing constant tends to
-four and the two laws converge in total variation.  This proves
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-count} and
-\eqref{eq:prime-support-inactive-window-law}.
-
-On compact subsets of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{d-1}\), the saddle remains in a
-compact subset of \(\prod_i(0,p_i^{-1})\), the transverse covariance stays
-uniformly nondegenerate, and the fixed-denominator bound supplies a common
-summable majorant for the cost tails.  The smooth-point expansions and all
-truncation estimates above are therefore uniform there.
-\end{proof}

-Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative

\section{Local fiber spectra and the critical Dirichlet law}
\label{sec:local-spectrum}

The pressure records only exponential growth.  On the proved frozen
half-line, a finer limit survives without exponential normalization.  It is
controlled by the fixed-level stabilization in the preceding section.

For \(m\ge1\) and \(k\ge1\), put
\[
 C_m(k):=\card{\{x\in X_m:d_m(x)=k\}},
 \qquad
 \nu_m:=\sum_{k\ge1}C_m(k)\delta_k.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Local microcanonical spectrum]
\label{thm:local-fiber-spectrum}
For every \(m\ge1\),
\[
 C_m(1)=2.
\]
The two singleton fibers have residues
\(F_{m+1}-1\) and \(F_{m+2}-1\).  For every \(k\ge2\),
\[
 C_m(k)\le4\Psi(k),
 \qquad
 C_m(k)=4\Psi(k)\quad(m\ge2k).
\]
In particular, \(C_m(2)=4\) for \(m\ge4\).  Moreover, the locally finite
measures \(\nu_m\) converge vaguely on the discrete space \(\mathbb N\) to
\[
 \nu_\infty=2\delta_1+4\sum_{k\ge2}\Psi(k)\delta_k.
\]
Equivalently, the masses of every finite subset of \(\mathbb N\) eventually
stabilize.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The fiber--partition interval identity gives, as multisets, the values of
\(R\) on the disjoint consecutive layers \(\mathcal I_m\) and
\(\mathcal I_{m+1}\).  Hence
\begin{equation}
 C_m(k)=N_m(k)+N_{m+1}(k).
 \label{eq:fiber-level-two-layer-count}
\end{equation}
The uniform layer-count lemma gives one value equal to \(1\) in each layer,
the bound \(N_j(k)\le2\Psi(k)\) for \(k\ge2\), and equality for
\(j\ge2k\).  Summing the two layers proves all the asserted counts.  Under
the interval identity, the two level-one points are the left endpoints
\(F_{m+1}-1\) and \(F_{m+2}-1\); inspection of the two cases in
\Cref{thm:fiber-partition-interval} shows that these are also their fiber
residues.  Finally, every compact subset of the discrete space
\(\mathbb N\) is finite, and each of its point masses eventually has the
displayed value.  This is precisely vague convergence.
\end{proof}

Define the unnormalized limiting spectral partition function by
\[
 \mathcal Z(s):=\frac{4}{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-2
 \qquad(s>\sigma_0).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact negative-tilt spectral limit]
\label{thm:spectral-partition-function}
For every \(s>\sigma_0\),
\[
 \lim_{m\to\infty}S_{-s}(m)=\mathcal Z(s)<\infty.
\]
For an arbitrary real tilt \(t\), the exact dichotomy is
\[
 \begin{cases}
 S_t(m)\longrightarrow
 \displaystyle\frac{4}{2-\zeta(-t-1)/\zeta(-t)}-2,&t< -\sigma_0,\\[8pt]
 S_t(m)\longrightarrow+\infty,&t\ge-\sigma_0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus \(-\sigma_0\) is the convergence boundary for the unnormalized
partition functions, independently of whether it is the boundary of the
zero-pressure set.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For \(s>\sigma_0\), \Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum} and dominated convergence
give
\[
 S_{-s}(m)
 =\sum_{k\ge1}C_m(k)k^{-s}
 \longrightarrow
 2+4\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^s}.
\]
The domination follows from \(C_m(k)\le4\Psi(k)\) for \(k\ge2\), and the
majorant is summable by
\eqref{eq:weinstein-level-dirichlet-series}.  Weinstein's Dirichlet identity
then reduces the last expression to \(\mathcal Z(s)\).

Suppose next that \(0<s\le\sigma_0\).  If \(2<s\le\sigma_0\), the geometric
series in \eqref{eq:weinstein-level-dirichlet-series} diverges.  If
\(0<s\le2\), the one-factor generating words give
\(\Psi(k)\ge\phi_{\rm E}(k)\), and the totient Dirichlet series diverges.
Thus \(\sum_{k\ge2}\Psi(k)k^{-s}=+\infty\) throughout this range.  For each
fixed \(K\), \Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum} gives, once \(m\ge2K\),
\[
 S_{-s}(m)\ge2+4\sum_{2\le k\le K}\Psi(k)k^{-s}.
\]
Letting \(K\to\infty\) proves divergence for
\(-\sigma_0\le t<0\).  For \(t\ge0\), nonempty fibers satisfy
\(d_m(x)^t\ge1\), and hence
\(S_t(m)\ge\card{X_m}=F_{m+2}\to\infty\).
\end{proof}

The singularity of \(\mathcal Z\) also determines a limiting Gibbs law.  Put
\[
 \kappa:=-\left.\frac{d}{ds}\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}
          \right|_{s=\sigma_0}
 =\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)\log n}{n^{\sigma_0}}
 =2.589184379946924\ldots.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Critical Gibbs spectrum]
\label{thm:critical-gibbs-spectrum}
As \(s\downarrow\sigma_0\),
\[
 \mathcal Z(s)=\frac{4}{\kappa(s-\sigma_0)}+O(1).
\]
For \(s>\sigma_0\), define
\[
 Q_{m,s}(k):=\frac{C_m(k)k^{-s}}{S_{-s}(m)}.
\]
Then \(Q_{m,s}\) converges in total variation to the probability measure
\[
 Q_s(1)=\frac2{\mathcal Z(s)},
 \qquad
 Q_s(k)=\frac{4\Psi(k)k^{-s}}{\mathcal Z(s)}\quad(k\ge2).
\]
In particular,
\[
 Q_s(1)\sim\frac\kappa2(s-\sigma_0).
\]
If \(K\) has law \(Q_s\), then
\[
 \mathbb E_s[\log K]
 =\frac1{s-\sigma_0}+O(1),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_s(\log K)
 =\frac1{(s-\sigma_0)^2}+O(1).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The totient series is absolutely differentiable in a neighborhood of
\(\sigma_0>2\), and therefore
\[
 2-\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}
 =\kappa(s-\sigma_0)+O((s-\sigma_0)^2).
\]
The pole expansion and the asymptotic for \(Q_s(1)\) follow.  For fixed
\(s>\sigma_0\), the pointwise convergence and summable domination used in
\Cref{thm:spectral-partition-function} give convergence of the unnormalized
weights in \(\ell^1(\mathbb N)\).  Normalizing therefore gives total
variation convergence.

Absolute differentiation of the limiting Dirichlet series yields
\[
 -\frac{d}{ds}\log\mathcal Z(s)=\mathbb E_s[\log K],
 \qquad
 \frac{d^2}{ds^2}\log\mathcal Z(s)
 =\operatorname{Var}_s(\log K).
\]
Since the denominator defining \(\mathcal Z\) is analytic at \(\sigma_0\)
and has a simple zero there, its Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \log\mathcal Z(s)
 =-\log(s-\sigma_0)+\log(4/\kappa)+O(s-\sigma_0),
\]
where the remainder is analytic.  Differentiating this local analytic
expansion proves the two moment estimates.
\end{proof}

The same pole has a Tauberian consequence for the generating-orbit counts.

\begin{theorem}[Generating-orbit Tauberian law]
\label{thm:psi-tauberian}
As \(x\to\infty\),
\[
 \sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)
 \sim\frac{x^{\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0\kappa},
 \qquad
 \sum_{k\le x}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^{\sigma_0}}
 \sim\frac1\kappa\log x.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \left(\frac4\kappa+o(1)\right)\log m
 \le S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
 \le\left(\frac{2\log\varphi}{\kappa}+o(1)\right)m.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Set
\[
 A(s)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)}{n^s}
 =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}-1.
\]
For \(\Re s>\sigma_0\), Weinstein's identity reads
\[
 1+\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^s}=\frac1{1-A(s)}.
\]
On the line \(\Re s=\sigma_0\), if \(\tau\ne0\), then
\[
 |A(\sigma_0+i\tau)|<A(\sigma_0)=1.
\]
Indeed, equality in the triangle inequality would force all
\(n^{-i\tau}\) with \(n\ge2\) to have the same phase; since the sum would
have to equal the positive number \(1\), it would in particular force
\(2^{-i\tau}=3^{-i\tau}=1\).  This contradicts
\(\log2/\log3\notin\mathbb Q\).  Thus the Dirichlet series has no other
boundary singularity and has at \(s=\sigma_0\) a simple pole of residue
\(1/\kappa\).  The Wiener--Ikehara theorem
\cite{Korevaar2004} now gives
\[
 \sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)
 \sim\frac{x^{\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0\kappa}.
\]
Partial summation gives the second asymptotic.

For the critical finite-window sum, stabilization gives
\[
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
 \ge2+4\sum_{2\le k\le m/2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^{\sigma_0}},
\]
which proves the lower bound.  The uniform layer estimate and the absence of
levels above \(D_m\) give
\[
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
 \le2+4\sum_{2\le k\le D_m}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^{\sigma_0}}.
\]
Now use the second Tauberian asymptotic and
\(\log D_m\sim\tfrac12m\log\varphi\).
\end{proof}

Finally, the same estimates narrow the possible location of the zero-pressure
boundary.  Write \(p_m(t)=m^{-1}\log S_t(m)\), and set
\[
 \beta_*:=\frac{\log\varphi}{\log(2/\varphi)}
 =2.270559453959664\ldots.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Pressure bounds in the transition strip]
\label{thm:pressure-transition-strip}
For \(0<s<\sigma_0\),
\[
 \max\left\{0,\log\varphi-s\log\frac2\varphi\right\}
 \le\liminf_{m\to\infty}p_m(-s)
\]
and
\[
 \limsup_{m\to\infty}p_m(-s)
 \le\min\left\{\log\varphi,
       \frac{\sigma_0-s}{2}\log\varphi\right\}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}p_m(t)>0\qquad(t>-\beta_*).
\]
Together with \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing}, this confines any
boundary of the zero-pressure set to
\[
 [-\sigma_0,-\beta_*]
 =[-2.478750785733960\ldots,-2.270559453959664\ldots].
\]
The width of this candidate strip is
\[
 \sigma_0-\beta_*=0.208191331774296\ldots.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Under the uniform distribution on \(X_m\), the mean fiber multiplicity is
\(2^m/F_{m+2}\).  Since \(u\mapsto u^{-s}\) is convex, Jensen's inequality
gives
\[
 \frac{S_{-s}(m)}{F_{m+2}}
 \ge\left(\frac{2^m}{F_{m+2}}\right)^{-s}.
\]
After taking logarithms and dividing by \(m\), this gives the nonzero term in
the lower bound; the term zero follows from the two singleton fibers.

For the upper bound, fix \(a>\sigma_0\).  Since all occurring levels satisfy
\(k\le D_m\), \Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum} gives
\[
 S_{-s}(m)
 \le2+4D_m^{a-s}\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^a}.
\]
Using \(m^{-1}\log D_m\to\tfrac12\log\varphi\) and then letting
\(a\downarrow\sigma_0\) proves the second term in the upper bound.  The
first follows directly from \(d_m(x)^{-s}\le1\).  If
\(-\beta_*<t<0\), the lower bound is strictly positive by the definition of
\(\beta_*\); if \(t\ge0\), then \(S_t(m)\ge F_{m+2}\).  This proves the
last assertion without assuming that the pressure limit exists.
\end{proof}

+\section{Local fiber spectra and the critical Dirichlet law}
+\label{sec:local-spectrum}
+
+The pressure records only exponential growth.  On the proved frozen
+half-line, a finer limit survives without exponential normalization.  It is
+controlled by the fixed-level stabilization in the preceding section.
+
+For \(m\ge1\) and \(k\ge1\), put
+\[
+ C_m(k):=\card{\{x\in X_m:d_m(x)=k\}},
+ \qquad
+ \nu_m:=\sum_{k\ge1}C_m(k)\delta_k.
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[Local microcanonical spectrum]
+\label{thm:local-fiber-spectrum}
+For every \(m\ge1\),
+\[
+ C_m(1)=2.
+\]
+The two singleton fibers have residues
+\(F_{m+1}-1\) and \(F_{m+2}-1\).  For every \(k\ge2\),
+\[
+ C_m(k)\le4\Psi(k),
+ \qquad
+ C_m(k)=4\Psi(k)\quad(m\ge2k).
+\]
+In particular, \(C_m(2)=4\) for \(m\ge4\).  Moreover, the locally finite
+measures \(\nu_m\) converge vaguely on the discrete space \(\mathbb N\) to
+\[
+ \nu_\infty=2\delta_1+4\sum_{k\ge2}\Psi(k)\delta_k.
+\]
+Equivalently, the masses of every finite subset of \(\mathbb N\) eventually
+stabilize.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The fiber--partition interval identity gives, as multisets, the values of
+\(R\) on the disjoint consecutive layers \(\mathcal I_m\) and
+\(\mathcal I_{m+1}\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}
+ C_m(k)=N_m(k)+N_{m+1}(k).
+ \label{eq:fiber-level-two-layer-count}
+\end{equation}
+The uniform layer-count lemma gives one value equal to \(1\) in each layer,
+the bound \(N_j(k)\le2\Psi(k)\) for \(k\ge2\), and equality for
+\(j\ge2k\).  Summing the two layers proves all the asserted counts.  Under
+the interval identity, the two level-one points are the left endpoints
+\(F_{m+1}-1\) and \(F_{m+2}-1\); inspection of the two cases in
+\Cref{thm:fiber-partition-interval} shows that these are also their fiber
+residues.  Finally, every compact subset of the discrete space
+\(\mathbb N\) is finite, and each of its point masses eventually has the
+displayed value.  This is precisely vague convergence.
+\end{proof}
+
+Define the unnormalized limiting spectral partition function by
+\[
+ \mathcal Z(s):=\frac{4}{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-2
+ \qquad(s>\sigma_0).
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[Exact negative-tilt spectral limit]
+\label{thm:spectral-partition-function}
+For every \(s>\sigma_0\),
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}S_{-s}(m)=\mathcal Z(s)<\infty.
+\]
+For an arbitrary real tilt \(t\), the exact dichotomy is
+\[
+ \begin{cases}
+ S_t(m)\longrightarrow
+ \displaystyle\frac{4}{2-\zeta(-t-1)/\zeta(-t)}-2,&t< -\sigma_0,\\[8pt]
+ S_t(m)\longrightarrow+\infty,&t\ge-\sigma_0.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+Thus \(-\sigma_0\) is the convergence boundary for the unnormalized
+partition functions, independently of whether it is the boundary of the
+zero-pressure set.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For \(s>\sigma_0\), \Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum} and dominated convergence
+give
+\[
+ S_{-s}(m)
+ =\sum_{k\ge1}C_m(k)k^{-s}
+ \longrightarrow
+ 2+4\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^s}.
+\]
+The domination follows from \(C_m(k)\le4\Psi(k)\) for \(k\ge2\), and the
+majorant is summable by
+\eqref{eq:weinstein-level-dirichlet-series}.  Weinstein's Dirichlet identity
+then reduces the last expression to \(\mathcal Z(s)\).
+
+Suppose next that \(0<s\le\sigma_0\).  If \(2<s\le\sigma_0\), the geometric
+series in \eqref{eq:weinstein-level-dirichlet-series} diverges.  If
+\(0<s\le2\), the one-factor generating words give
+\(\Psi(k)\ge\phi_{\rm E}(k)\), and the totient Dirichlet series diverges.
+Thus \(\sum_{k\ge2}\Psi(k)k^{-s}=+\infty\) throughout this range.  For each
+fixed \(K\), \Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum} gives, once \(m\ge2K\),
+\[
+ S_{-s}(m)\ge2+4\sum_{2\le k\le K}\Psi(k)k^{-s}.
+\]
+Letting \(K\to\infty\) proves divergence for
+\(-\sigma_0\le t<0\).  For \(t\ge0\), nonempty fibers satisfy
+\(d_m(x)^t\ge1\), and hence
+\(S_t(m)\ge\card{X_m}=F_{m+2}\to\infty\).
+\end{proof}
+
+The singularity of \(\mathcal Z\) also determines a limiting Gibbs law.  Put
+\[
+ \kappa:=-\left.\frac{d}{ds}\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}
+          \right|_{s=\sigma_0}
+ =\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)\log n}{n^{\sigma_0}}
+ =2.589184379946924\ldots.
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[Critical Gibbs spectrum]
+\label{thm:critical-gibbs-spectrum}
+As \(s\downarrow\sigma_0\),
+\[
+ \mathcal Z(s)=\frac{4}{\kappa(s-\sigma_0)}+O(1).
+\]
+For \(s>\sigma_0\), define
+\[
+ Q_{m,s}(k):=\frac{C_m(k)k^{-s}}{S_{-s}(m)}.
+\]
+Then \(Q_{m,s}\) converges in total variation to the probability measure
+\[
+ Q_s(1)=\frac2{\mathcal Z(s)},
+ \qquad
+ Q_s(k)=\frac{4\Psi(k)k^{-s}}{\mathcal Z(s)}\quad(k\ge2).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ Q_s(1)\sim\frac\kappa2(s-\sigma_0).
+\]
+If \(K\) has law \(Q_s\), then
+\[
+ \mathbb E_s[\log K]
+ =\frac1{s-\sigma_0}+O(1),
+ \qquad
+ \operatorname{Var}_s(\log K)
+ =\frac1{(s-\sigma_0)^2}+O(1).
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The totient series is absolutely differentiable in a neighborhood of
+\(\sigma_0>2\), and therefore
+\[
+ 2-\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}
+ =\kappa(s-\sigma_0)+O((s-\sigma_0)^2).
+\]
+The pole expansion and the asymptotic for \(Q_s(1)\) follow.  For fixed
+\(s>\sigma_0\), the pointwise convergence and summable domination used in
+\Cref{thm:spectral-partition-function} give convergence of the unnormalized
+weights in \(\ell^1(\mathbb N)\).  Normalizing therefore gives total
+variation convergence.
+
+Absolute differentiation of the limiting Dirichlet series yields
+\[
+ -\frac{d}{ds}\log\mathcal Z(s)=\mathbb E_s[\log K],
+ \qquad
+ \frac{d^2}{ds^2}\log\mathcal Z(s)
+ =\operatorname{Var}_s(\log K).
+\]
+Since the denominator defining \(\mathcal Z\) is analytic at \(\sigma_0\)
+and has a simple zero there, its Taylor expansion gives
+\[
+ \log\mathcal Z(s)
+ =-\log(s-\sigma_0)+\log(4/\kappa)+O(s-\sigma_0),
+\]
+where the remainder is analytic.  Differentiating this local analytic
+expansion proves the two moment estimates.
+\end{proof}
+
+The same pole has a Tauberian consequence for the generating-orbit counts.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Generating-orbit Tauberian law]
+\label{thm:psi-tauberian}
+As \(x\to\infty\),
+\[
+ \sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)
+ \sim\frac{x^{\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0\kappa},
+ \qquad
+ \sum_{k\le x}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^{\sigma_0}}
+ \sim\frac1\kappa\log x.
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ \left(\frac4\kappa+o(1)\right)\log m
+ \le S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ \le\left(\frac{2\log\varphi}{\kappa}+o(1)\right)m.
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Set
+\[
+ A(s)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(n)}{n^s}
+ =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}-1.
+\]
+For \(\Re s>\sigma_0\), Weinstein's identity reads
+\[
+ 1+\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^s}=\frac1{1-A(s)}.
+\]
+On the line \(\Re s=\sigma_0\), if \(\tau\ne0\), then
+\[
+ |A(\sigma_0+i\tau)|<A(\sigma_0)=1.
+\]
+Indeed, equality in the triangle inequality would force all
+\(n^{-i\tau}\) with \(n\ge2\) to have the same phase; since the sum would
+have to equal the positive number \(1\), it would in particular force
+\(2^{-i\tau}=3^{-i\tau}=1\).  This contradicts
+\(\log2/\log3\notin\mathbb Q\).  Thus the Dirichlet series has no other
+boundary singularity and has at \(s=\sigma_0\) a simple pole of residue
+\(1/\kappa\).  The Wiener--Ikehara theorem
+\cite{Korevaar2004} now gives
+\[
+ \sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)
+ \sim\frac{x^{\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0\kappa}.
+\]
+Partial summation gives the second asymptotic.
+
+For the critical finite-window sum, stabilization gives
+\[
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ \ge2+4\sum_{2\le k\le m/2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^{\sigma_0}},
+\]
+which proves the lower bound.  The uniform layer estimate and the absence of
+levels above \(D_m\) give
+\[
+ S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
+ \le2+4\sum_{2\le k\le D_m}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^{\sigma_0}}.
+\]
+Now use the second Tauberian asymptotic and
+\(\log D_m\sim\tfrac12m\log\varphi\).
+\end{proof}
+
+Finally, the same estimates narrow the possible location of the zero-pressure
+boundary.  Write \(p_m(t)=m^{-1}\log S_t(m)\), and set
+\[
+ \beta_*:=\frac{\log\varphi}{\log(2/\varphi)}
+ =2.270559453959664\ldots.
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[Pressure bounds in the transition strip]
+\label{thm:pressure-transition-strip}
+For \(0<s<\sigma_0\),
+\[
+ \max\left\{0,\log\varphi-s\log\frac2\varphi\right\}
+ \le\liminf_{m\to\infty}p_m(-s)
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \limsup_{m\to\infty}p_m(-s)
+ \le\min\left\{\log\varphi,
+       \frac{\sigma_0-s}{2}\log\varphi\right\}.
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \liminf_{m\to\infty}p_m(t)>0\qquad(t>-\beta_*).
+\]
+Together with \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing}, this confines any
+boundary of the zero-pressure set to
+\[
+ [-\sigma_0,-\beta_*]
+ =[-2.478750785733960\ldots,-2.270559453959664\ldots].
+\]
+The width of this candidate strip is
+\[
+ \sigma_0-\beta_*=0.208191331774296\ldots.
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Under the uniform distribution on \(X_m\), the mean fiber multiplicity is
+\(2^m/F_{m+2}\).  Since \(u\mapsto u^{-s}\) is convex, Jensen's inequality
+gives
+\[
+ \frac{S_{-s}(m)}{F_{m+2}}
+ \ge\left(\frac{2^m}{F_{m+2}}\right)^{-s}.
+\]
+After taking logarithms and dividing by \(m\), this gives the nonzero term in
+the lower bound; the term zero follows from the two singleton fibers.
+
+For the upper bound, fix \(a>\sigma_0\).  Since all occurring levels satisfy
+\(k\le D_m\), \Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum} gives
+\[
+ S_{-s}(m)
+ \le2+4D_m^{a-s}\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{\Psi(k)}{k^a}.
+\]
+Using \(m^{-1}\log D_m\to\tfrac12\log\varphi\) and then letting
+\(a\downarrow\sigma_0\) proves the second term in the upper bound.  The
+first follows directly from \(d_m(x)^{-s}\le1\).  If
+\(-\beta_*<t<0\), the lower bound is strictly positive by the definition of
+\(\beta_*\); if \(t\ge0\), then \(S_t(m)\ge F_{m+2}\).  This proves the
+last assertion without assuming that the pressure limit exists.
+\end{proof}
